title: Add VPC control plane Terraform module: subnets, endpoints, SGs, peering, Route53 delegation
author: Sofia Martinez
release_notes: Add new terraform module to provision Private Control Plane VPC resources (subnets, endpoints, security groups, peering, Route53 delegation). Backwards-compatible. Enables automated provisioning for on-prem/VPC private deployments.
description: Motivation: Add a reusable Terraform module to provision the Private Control Plane VPC and associated infra in AWS so customers using Redwood Private can automate control plane networking (subnets, endpoints, security groups), cross-account Route53 delegation for control-plane DNS zones, and VPC peering to tenant VPCs. This PR consolidates prior manual runbooks into codified, idempotent IaC. What changed (high-level): 1) modules/control-plane-vpc: new Terraform module that creates multi-az private subnets, NATs (optional), VPC endpoints for S3 and STS, and configurable endpoint policies; 2) modules/security: security-group templates tuned for control plane (least-priv outbound for Kubernetes nodes, tenants to control plane only on allowed ports); 3) route53-delegation: resources and example for cross-account hosted zone delegation and glue records to support private hosted zones; 4) peering: VPC peering configuration with automated route propagation/route table updates in examples; 5) examples/aws/control-plane-deploy: opinionated example using the module with inputs for hub account vs tenant account; 6) CI/ops: added terraform fmt/check and plan job for module, and unit tests with terratest harness skeleton. Design notes: - Module is single-purpose and exposes inputs for azs, cidr_blocks, enable_nat, endpoint_services, route53_zone_name, delegation_account_id, and tenancy tags. - By default endpoints created are com.amazonaws.<region>.s3 and sts; additional endpoints may be enabled by input list. - Security groups are template driven; default rules allow control plane management ports (6443, 10250) only from tenant CIDR blocks passed in via variables; admin CIDR can be configured separately. - For Route53 delegation we adopt cross-account NS record delegation into the tenant account and include an optional terraform data source to look up existing delegation. This avoids creating new public zones and keeps DNS private. Checklist (completed): - [x] Terraform module and README with usage and inputs/outputs - [x] Example deployment - [x] unit tests skeleton and CI plan job - [x] Security review by Priya (SG rules tightened) - [x] Manual test deploy in staging account and verification of DNS/peering and endpoints - [x] Update installer docs references Usage example (snippet): module "control_plane_vpc" { source = "../modules/control-plane-vpc" region = var.region azs = var.azs cidr_block = "10.100.0.0/16" tenant_cidrs = var.tenant_cidrs delegation_account_id = var.tenant_account enable_s3_endpoint = true } Testing performed: - Deployed to staging-hub (us-west-2) with two tenant VPCs. Verified: VPC peering established, routes propagated, S3 and STS endpoints reachable from control plane subnets only, security groups blocked all unexpected inbound traffic, Route53 private hosted zone resolvable from tenant VPC after delegation. - Ran terraform plan/apply in CI with mock variables to ensure idempotency. - Performed negative tests: denied delegation_account_id to simulate missing permissions; validated the plan fails with a meaningful error. Rollback / upgrade notes: - Module is additive and respects existing resources when import variables are provided. To rollback, run terraform apply with previous state; for cross-account delegation, remove NS delegation if rolling back DNS changes. - When upgrading existing control planes, specify existing VPC IDs and route table IDs to avoid replacement. Documented in examples/UPGRADING.md. Security considerations: - Endpoint policies default to least privilege; operators must review S3 endpoint policy if using cross-account S3 buckets. - SGs are explicit and do not use 0.0.0.0/0 for management ports. - IAM permissions required for cross-account Route53 delegation are documented in the module README. Related: Linear ENG-8842 (private deploy networking), INFRA-125 (terraform modules consolidation), incident SUP-342 referenced for previous manual runbook. Merge method: squash.
